props.title: The adversarial game
props.subtitle: Generator tries to fool the discriminator

items: G maps noise z → fake image
D classifies real vs fake
Train D to distinguish, G to fool
At equilibrium, D outputs 0.5 everywhere
In practice — balance is fragile
Transposed convs in G, strided convs in D
BatchNorm in both, LeakyReLU in D
No fully-connected layers, tanh output
Adam with β₁=0.5 — unstable at default 0.9

props.title: Mode collapse
props.subtitle: When G settles for a subset of the distribution

items: Symptom: repetitive samples, low diversity
Track per-class sample distribution during training
Mini-batch discrimination — D sees sample variance
Feature matching loss — match G to real statistics
Unrolled GAN — D lookahead prevents G gaming
Replace JS divergence with Earth-Mover distance
Critic (not discriminator) — linear output, no sigmoid
1-Lipschitz constraint: clip weights or use GP
Gradient penalty is the modern default
Loss actually correlates with sample quality
Concatenate class embedding to noise input
AC-GAN — auxiliary classifier head on D
Projection discriminator — cleaner conditioning
pix2pix / CycleGAN — image-to-image translation
Inception Score — rewards confidence and diversity
IS is domain-limited and gameable
FID — Fréchet distance between feature distributions
Lower FID = closer to real data — now the standard
Always report both IS and FID with sample size
